=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/review_merge_train.sh: line ~440, the --jq projection inside _mt_inflight_review_branches:
  `{total_count: .total_count, workflow_runs: (.workflow_runs | if type == "array" then [.[] | select(type == "object") | {id: .id, status: .status, event: .event, head_branch: .head_branch, display_title: .display_title, path: .path, created_at: .created_at}] else . end)}` | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The inner `select(type == "object")` silently drops non-object elements from `workflow_runs` before the page validator sees them.
  WHY: A malformed response can pass validation as a complete empty listing, allowing the train to dispatch a second review beside a pending one.
- scripts/review_merge_train.sh: line ~489, the per-run validator:
  `all(.workflow_runs[]; (.id | type == "number") and (.path | type == "string" and length > 0) and (.status | type == "string" and length > 0))` | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The validator does not require `event` to be a non-empty string, though downstream key construction uses it to attribute runs.
  WHY: A missing or null event can misclassify a dispatch run, allowing `_mt_release` to dispatch a duplicate review.
- Requirement: The completed plan document must consistently reflect the shipped behavior: all five non-terminal statuses are read twice, normally 10 API calls per release invocation, per auto-decision AD-15.
  Expected change site: docs/completed/issue-5443-merge-train-complete-run-listing-plan.md, Approach section (line 58) and Risks & Mitigations section (line 107).
  Evidence of absence: The top-of-document "As shipped" summary (lines 17-21) correctly states "the five statuses in lifecycle order, twice" and "API calls: normally 10 per release invocation". However, the inline parentheticals in the body are stale: line 58 reads "as shipped: five statuses, then all but `in_progress` again, AD-12 and AD-13" (describing the superseded 9-query AD-13 behavior), and line 107 reads "Lazy fetch: 0 calls when nothing is queued (previously 1), 3 when something is (as shipped: 9)" (describing the same superseded behavior with the old 3/9 call counts). Both inline notes contradict the "As shipped" summary and the shipped AD-15 implementation (10 calls, all five statuses twice).
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
